name: Takei et al. 2026 Cell Systems 17(11):101717, 'Genome-wide chromatin recording resolves dynamic cell state changes' (LagTag)
looked_at: 2026-11-27 (full text via PubMed Central; cell.com blocks automated reading)
what: records an earlier chromatin state (M.EcoGII adenine-methyltransferase fusions switched on by Shield-1 for 16 h) and reads it out later with the present state from the same ~10^4 cells (m6A antibody + CUT&Tag); marks dilute with division (robust ~2-3 divisions)
cells: mouse E14 ES cells; Gata4-induced endoderm, 24 h chase (~2 divisions)
result: recorded (before) signal at pluripotency genes (Zfp42), endpoint (after) at endoderm genes (Sox17); 933 genes change Pol II after differentiation

data.GEO: GSE305653 (raw and processed LagTag and CUT&Tag)

use_for_cellbrain: a lab method for our 'timing / next step' gap (before and after states of the same cells); its own data are small (mouse ES -> endoderm, 4 marks, bulk) and mostly mouse, so only a small before -> after test is possible now
